Seeded fruit products in general have been selected as the object of research, because their drying is difficult, due to the occurrence of many adverse effects in the heat treatment process, and they are of great interest to consumers and to companies in the processing and marketing of agricultural food products. The essential results obtained in the application of the developed installation to the drying of fruit products, with the application of the proposed technological processing method, are: reduction of electricity consumption and treatment time, increase of productivity and quality of the products. Moreover, the elaborate installation is simple in terms of construction, low in cost and easy to use. The installation also enables the drying process to be automated and, during research, has demonstrated a high degree of operational safety. The significance of the results obtained lies in the solution to a number of current problems faced by agricultural processing companies, in particular, the significant increase in the efficiency of the drying process of fruit products, based on the application of the microwave tunnel treatment process, mainly with an increase in energy efficiency and quality of the finished products.

articleTitle: Magnetic Circuit Segmentation Effects on Fractional Slot Concentrated Winding Synchronous Machine with Grain Oriented Electric Steel
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation on a fractional slot concentrated winding synchronous machine with wound rotor excitation, having different combination of non-oriented and grain oriented electric steel used for rotor poles and stator teeth and yoke. First, the effects of magnetic circuit segmentation are studied on the proposed structure with non-oriented electric steel, considering the small airgaps produced by this fabrication technique, and next, grain oriented electric steel is used for different parts of the rotor and stator magnetic circuit to evaluate the possibility of performance improvement. The purpose of this study is to find the most suitable structure for these types of machines to be build, from performance point of view, as well as material use and fabrication costs, by adopting a modular construction that reduces material wastes and increases the degree of automation of the manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Implementation of Hysteresis Current Controllers with Switching Frequency Limitation for Electric Traction Systems with Induction Motor and Rotor Field Orientation Control Using dSpace Prototyping Board
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The aim of this paper is the experimental validation of a switching frequency limiting system designated for hysteresis controllers used in closed loop current control. The system was used in a traction system for electric locomotives with voltage inverter and induction motor with rotor field orientation control. The system regulates the mean switching frequency with a proportional integrative controller which adapts the hysteresis band. The switching frequency control system has two inputs, the imposed mean switching frequency and the initial hysteresis band and one output, which is the actual hysteresis band. Consequently, the hysteresis current controller uses variable band comparators. The correct substantiation and implementation was experimentally validated on a full scale experimental traction system.

articleTitle: A Novel Sensorless Control of a Hybrid Excitation Synchronous Machine used in the Field of Electric Traction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The Dual Excitation Synchronous Machine, or so-called Hybrid Excitation Synchronous Machine (HESM), used to power traction vehicles are described in this work in general terms. The paper's second section compares several position speed observers mentioned in the literature along with a novel sensorless control technique for the HESM. The Matlab tool will be used to develop and analyze models and control techniques for HESM. In the final section of the work, conclusions and future research directions are presented.

articleTitle: Determination and Monitoring of the Overhead Electricity Transmission Cables Sag
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Based on the increased need in the last decade to accurately estimate sag value in overhead power transmission lines, a primary method of calculating cable sag value is presented in this article It presents the basic equations starting from the chain equation and the implementation of an offline algorithm developed in Matlab environment to obtain the cable sag value of the overhead power transmission lines. In addition, a minimal hardware/software architecture is presented, which uses in addition to the geometrical data of the power line the information provided by a specialized sensor to measure the horizontal mechanical stress in the cable. Improved versions of this hardware/software architecture, which require additional information from the tilt sensors of the cable, also allow the software implementation of a fault observer. The realtime software implementation for laboratory experiments is based on the LabVIEW programming environment.

articleTitle: Study and Design of a Teaching Electrical Engineering System Based on Motion Sensors Using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The aim of the paper is a didactic one considering this work useful for the students of Transylvania University of Brasov - Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences, the Department of Electrical Engineering and Applied Physics, at the courses Electrical Measurement and Data Acquisition. The disciplines are compulsory for our second-year students from the Electrical Engineering program from both, the Romanian and English language study programs of BA level. We start by covering a theoretical part including the principles of using measuring motion sensors, how they work and their role, as well as basic principles regarding the use of a servomotor and of the Arduino development board. After understanding the theory and practice of using the Arduino Board we present the actual experiment where 34 students were asked to answer a questionnaire highlighting how their learning and evaluation process was affected by the used method. The students were also asked to justify and explain their answers. We believe that by designing and implementing this method and application students will be able to put into practice the acquired theoretical knowledge, therefore the study could contribute to the improvement of the educational didactic process.

articleTitle: Current Regulation in Case of Open Circuit Fault for Six-phase Traction Open-end Winding Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The electric aircraft propulsion system should comply high safety standards and implement fault tolerant operation in case of partial failures. The fault tolerant operation is enabled due to both hardware and control. The paper considers the six-phase permanent magnet propulsion motor with open-end winding configuration. The open circuit fault in a single phase is the most common fault when it is possible to continue producing the same torque by changing the current references in other phases. The paper proposes the method of forming the referenced current vector with the help of the phases left in operation. It is shown that the increase in the current magnitude by 23.6% is required, whereas the simple increase of the currents by 20% produces the same average torque over the revolution with 20% torque pulsation. As the torque pulsations may cause the mechanical resonance and failure of the propeller, the proposed method is advisable even having a little bit higher ohmic losses.

articleTitle: Optimization of Cylindrical Blades for Wind Turbine Based on Magnus Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Wind turbines based on the Magnus effect open new prospects in terms of energy generation for areas with low average wind speeds. The main feature of these turbines is rotating cylinders which are used to create lift instead of blades. Due to this unconventional design, different parameters of the cylinder, such as mass and moment of inertia, can greatly affect the dynamic characteristics of such energy systems. The goal of this paper was to present an approach to structural optimization of a cylinder flange of the experimental Magnus effect-based wind turbine. The proposed approach, presented as an algorithm, allows us to determine input data for the preferred structural optimization software and achieve lightweight, low-inertia parts. Control simulation has shown that optimized parts ensure a high enough factor of safety while also significantly reducing the moment of inertia.

articleTitle: Equipment and Methodology for Detecting Clearance in Front Suspension Joints of Passenger Vehicles by Using Dynamic Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative system designed to detect the existence of clearance in the joints of front suspension and steering systems of passenger vehicles. The system employs dynamic acceleration analysis by tilting the motor vehicle chassis using a pneumatic actuator and utilizes accelerometers to detect the existence of clearance at various points in the suspension and steering components. The research showcases the development and application of the system, supported by advanced data acquisition (DAQ) technology and a comprehensive methodology. Experimental data is collected in realtime and processed using LabViewsoftware, with results visualized through acceleration, velocity, and position graphs. Furthermore, a Bode plot provides insight into the behavior of accelerations at different frequencies, aiding in the objective assessment of the front suspension joints' condition. The outcomes of the study provide valuable insights into enhancing motor vehicle maintenance and improving the performance of suspension and steering systems. Further investigations could delve into additional factors influencing joint wear and refine the analysis methodology.

articleTitle: Power Quality Considering the Massive Integration of Variable Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Signing Paris Agreement and European Green Deal, European Union committed to becoming a carbon emission-neutral continent by 2050 in terms of GHG. The Republic of Moldova is the European Union Associated Country, a member of the European Energy Community, and a signatory part of the Paris Agreement. Thus, the Republic of Moldova took commitments to reduce its carbon emissions too. The Republic of Moldova has substantial renewable energy sources potential, especially wind, solar, and bioenergy. Integration of wind and solar energy sources (variable renewable energy sources) is associated with several technical, economic, social, and environmental challenges, including reliability and resilience of the energy systems and the power quality, etc. Considering the projected energy transition, this paper presents the analysis of risks for power quality in the massive presence of variable renewable energy sources in the National Power System.

articleTitle: Testing the Interaction of Electromagnetic Radiation with Nano/Micro-Conductive Composite Material
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The article highlights the fact that testing the interaction of electromagnetic radiation with matter, within nano/micro-conductive composites, can be highlighted by measuring dielectric properties such as permittivity, loss tangent and conductivity, because the amount of electrical energy stored in the electric field depends on the degree of polarization that occurs when a certain voltage is applied to a material. In many fields and applications, such as optics, spectroscopy, medical imaging, communications, power electronics, and many others, the interaction of electromagnetic radiation with matter is essential. This interaction process is beneficial for the creation of innovative materials and technologies, as well as their application in a variety of scientific and technological fields.

articleTitle: Designing of Variable Input Multiphase Buck Converter with Efficient Phase Current Balancing Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Phase current imbalance issues with multiphase DC/DC converters are well-known. The main cause is due to the non-ideal characteristics of each leg component and driver, including MOSFET conduction resistance, driver delay, and passive circuits. Each leg's current imbalance reduces the efficiency, stability, and dependability of multiphase converters and also harms switching transistors and results in inductor saturation. The proposed phase current balancing technique utilized in this study validates the electromagnetic interference prevention while being straightforward and simple to use. The dynamic load switching control mechanism is also included in the suggested model.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis and Experimental Validation of a Series Hybrid Excitation Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Numerical analysis, using Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations, of a series hybrid excitation synchronous machine (HESM), along with experimental test results are presented into this paper. The proposed machine consists of a distributed three-phase winding placed into the 36 stator slots and a four poles rotor from which two are with surface mounted permanent magnets and the other two hosts field excitation coils. This way, the advantages of permanent magnet and electromagnetic excitation of synchronous machines are combined, providing both high efficiency and flexibility. The particularities of the working characteristics of such a machine are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing the Optimization of Magnetically Coupled Coil Structures-Analysis and Discussions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The paper explores the factors influencing the optimization of magnetically coupled coil structures through in-depth analysis and discussions. Optimizing the wireless power transfer system (WPTS) is crucial as it enhances the efficiency, reliability, and overall performance of the system, leading to more effective and sustainable wireless energy transmission solutions. The optimization process involves considering multiple aspects, such as coil structure, configuration, number of turns, coil shape, working frequencies, electromagnetic properties of the medium, and coil distance. To identify the relevant parameters (R, L, C, and G) for a system consisting of two magnetically coupled coils used WPTS, advanced electromagnetic field numerical simulation software is employed. Among the widely utilized software tools for estimating the parameters of electromagnetic systems is the ANSYS Q3D EXTRACTOR, available in both 2D and 3D versions.

articleTitle: Determination of Wind Characteristics for Different Heights Based on Digital Maps of the Wind Potential of the Republic of Moldova
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The paper presents the calculation method for determining the wind characteristics for different heights based on developed digital maps of wind energy potential. Data on wind characteristics determined from digital maps of wind energy potential that are developed only for heights of 50 and 100 m above ground level are used to calculate wind parameters: average wind speed, wind power density and coefficients of the Weibull analytical approximation A and k, for any height between 10 and 150 m. The obtained data can serve as input data for the calculation of electrical or thermal energy production by a wind turbine.

articleTitle: Loop Closing of Flyback Switching Power Supply Using Capacitive Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This article demonstrates the functionality of a switching power supply employing the flyback topology with a capacitive closed control loop. The laboratory implementation of the Switched Mode Power Supply (SMPS) is presented, highlighting the importance of capacitive coupling for achieving efficient power transfer while maintaining necessary isolation and safety between interconnected modules. To showcase the operational capabilities of the switching power supply, an illustrative and experimental module has been developed, employing capacitive coupling to establish the feedback loop. The use of the flyback topology ensures galvanic separation, enhancing the overall performance of the system. The module is structured into two main components: the primary module and the secondary module. Experimental determinations encompass various aspects, including the testing of capacitive coupling using an AB class amplifier driver. Additionally, the delay times for both optical and capacitive couplings are determined through experimentation. The rise time and fall time between the capacitive coupling and the optical coupling are also examined. The results of these experiments shed light on the advantages and limitations of capacitive coupling compared to optical coupling in the context of the switching power supply. The findings presented in this article contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the benefits and performance characteristics associated with capacitive coupling and optical coupling in practice.

articleTitle: Modified Schemes of Control and Multi-Zone PWM of Diode-Clamped Inverters of Drive Installations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The paper presents short overview of the development and dissemination of an alternative method of control and synchronous multi-zone pulsewidth modulation (SMZ PWM), founded on space vector principles, for the adjustment of diode-clamped inverters (DCINs) with relatively low switching frequency (SwFr) of three-phase (3ph) and six-phase (6ph) adjustable speed drive installations. It insures providing both synchronization and symmetry of the basic voltages and minimization of common mode voltage (CMV) in drive installations. Examples of the use of this method to adjustment several topologies of DCIN-based ac drives are presented.

articleTitle: Complementary Analysis of the Fault Condition of Transformers in Service
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper presents a complementary analysis of the fault condition of the transformers, based on Duval triangles 1, 4 and 5 for the detection of the basic fault. The analysis of carbon oxides and furan compounds was used to determine the state of degradation of the solid insulation. The method presented in this paper deals especially with the case where the defect involves high temperatures and paper carbonization, and the results were concrete and accurate. The results obtained with this method demonstrate the importance of the collaboration of analysis methods.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Between Distributed and Fractional Slot Concentrated Winding of a Wound Rotor Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: A comparative analysis between distributed winding (DW) and fractional slot concentrated winding (FSCW) synchronous machine with electromagnetic excitation is presented in this paper. The main interest is to highlight the advantages brought by using FSCW over DW synchronous machines in terms of both efficiency and fabrication costs, for certain applications such as wind turbine, hydro generation, automotive, industries in continuous development. For those reasons, an 8 poles synchronous machine is studied in both cases, with 72 stator slots for the DW structure and 9 stator coils for the FSCW structure respectively, with the same dimensional constrains and rotor architecture, for comparation. Simulation results using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) are analyzed, and conclusions are presented.

articleTitle: Inner-Rotor And Outer-Rotor PMSG Designs for Novel Offshore Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed design methodology for the inner and outer rotor structures of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators (PMSGs) for the novel X-rotor offshore wind turbine concept. For the X-rotor system, the design results are evaluated in terms of efficiency, power factor, weight, and temperature rise. ANSYS electromagnetic and thermal simulations are used for further validation. Inner rotor machines cause less heat to be dissipated, while outer rotor machines are lighter, have the highest power density, and have the smallest outer diameter and losses. Results from this research can be applied to applications that require electric machines that are lighter, more powerful, and have improved thermal performance.

articleTitle: Dedicated Analog Circuit Simulation Programs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper has as a main purpose the presentation of three dedicated programs for analog circuit simulation, developed by the research team at University Politehnica of Bucharest (UPB): Circuit Symbolic Analysis Program (CSAP), Transfer Function Symbolic Generation (TFSYG), and SYmbolic State Equation Generation (SYSEG). These dedicated programs present a series of advantages as compared to the commercial software (e.g. SPICE). The article exposes the steps for using the afore-mentioned programs and how to analyze the obtained results. Examples of various circuit structures are given for each type of analysis. Some examples are analyzed in parallel with the SPICE program to check the accuracy of the obtained results.

articleTitle: Cost-Benefit Analysis for Renewable Energy Generation in a Hotel-type Building
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The aim of this project is to assess the costs and benefits associated with the implementation of an integrated system consisting of a photovoltaic system and a heat pump in a tourist pension building. The choice between this integrated solution and the option with a wood-fired boiler will be made based on a cost-benefit analysis. Through the implementation of this system, the goal is to provide a renewable and efficient source of energy to cover the electricity, heating, and hot water needs of the building. Additionally, it aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, thereby contributing to environmental protection and combating climate change. The cost-benefit analysis will evaluate both the initial investment costs for the acquisition of equipment and the long-term operating and maintenance costs. On the benefits side, savings obtained from using renewable energy instead of fossil fuels will be taken into account, as well as possible subsidies or financial incentives for such eco-friendly solutions. By comparing the two options and evaluating the results of the cost-benefit analysis, an informed decision will be made regarding the most viable and cost-effective energy system for the hotel-type building.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Controller Tuning Methods for Second-Order Time Delayed Object Model with Astatism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of the tuning procedures of the control algorithms for a second-order time delayed control object model with astatism with known parameters using the methods of maximal stability degree with iterations and polynomial approach. For tuning the controller parameters for the second-order time delayed control object model with astatism with known parameters, a procedure using the maximal stability degree method with iterations is developed. Analytical expressions for the controller tuning parameters are obtained as nonlinear functions of the stability degree argument and the known object parameters. The stability degree is varied, and these functions are graphically constructed. Through iterative procedures along these curves, sets of controller parameter values are selected for the same argument value. Performance analysis and system robustness are established through simulation, aiming to achieve the highest results. A control algorithm synthesis procedure is developed using the modified polynomial method. To verify and compare the obtained results, an example is studied based on the proposed methods. The application of pole-zero method and parametric optimization are performed, and system simulations are conducted on a computer to analyze performance. The control object model parameters are varied within ±50 % of the nominal values, and system robustness is verified. The advantages of the maximal stability degree method with reduced calculations and minimal time and the modified polynomial method are highlighted, simplifying the controller parameter tuning process for these object models.

Author Keywords: second-order delayed and astatism control object model

articleTitle: Test-Based Analysis of Fault Tolerance Capability of Six-Phase Asynchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Six-phase asynchronous motors are becoming increasingly popular in transport and industrial applications due to their advantages such as less torque ripple, better power distribution between the phases, higher efficiency, and increased tolerance capability errors compared to three-phase ones. This paper presents an analysis, primarily based on the results of experimental tests but also on theoretical arguments, of the natural fault tolerance capacity of an asynchronous motor (induction machines) in six phases with symmetrical and asymmetrical windings. The degree of tolerance is examined, defined as the ability of the machine to create a starting and overload torque and to withstand operation for a certain period of time without danger to the integrity and reduction of the life resource of the insulation. A matrix of tolerance rating is defined regarding the operation of the motor on loss of supply on one, two or three phases in different sequences.

articleTitle: Availability of Hydroelectric Generating Units based on the Maintenance Schedule
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The paper uses the technique called “frequency and duration”, a continuous-time Markov chain, for evaluation of availability and reliability indicators of a hydroelectric power station using the operational data spanning 12 years (2010 ÷2021). The availability and reliability of individual units and for the entire power station are evaluated using failure rate λ, repair rate µ, Mean Time To Repair, Mean Time Between Failures, Mean Time To Failure, state probability, state frequency and departure rate.

articleTitle: Considerations on the Behaviour of Protective Clothing Against the Thermal Hazards Caused by an Electric Arc
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: This paper presents an overview over the experimental research on the behavior of the protective clothing against the thermal hazards of an electric arc. It studies the behavior of the garments (new or prewashed, intended for use in electrotechnical networks where risks of electric arc exist) at a directed and constrained electric arc. A practical scenario has been selected with constructive, electrical and test parameters setup. The test results were studied and were made observations over the impact of the test arc regarding the effects produced by gas cloud and plasma by radiation and convection or by direct contact and hot molten metal particles and splash. The setup and experimental test box were designed to meet the typical arc fault conditions and to cover actual arc exposure conditions in electrical equipment and installations were the electric arc is directed to the front of the worker at the height of his breastbone.

articleTitle: Simulating the Interaction of Electromagnetic Radiation with Matter, Within Nano/Micro-Conductive Composite
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The article aims to simulate the interaction of electromagnetic radiation with composite materials, based on PE filled with conductive particles (type A and B), when subjected to the electromagnetic field, using specialized CST Studio software. Using the Nicolson, Ross, Weir procedure in vacuum, a plane electromagnetic wave was applied to the polymer nanocomposite material to be able to calculate the volumetric density of the absorbed power and the specific absorption rate (SAR) for models with a uniform and random distribution of inserts.

articleTitle: Determining the Occupancy Patterns and Typical Power Demand Profiles of the Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Using a Flexible Clustering-based Data Mining Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Due to the increasing number of electric vehicle charging events, an enormous data volume can be generated and recorded in very large databases. A deeper analysis of the data collected by the monitoring systems could provide significant information to characterize the behavior of the electric vehicle charging stations. Unfortunately, the features of occupancy patterns or the typical power demand profiles corresponding to the charging stations are many and various and can be hard to identify and interpret without adequate techniques. In this context, a flexible clustering-based data mining framework has been proposed to extract the main features (the number of hours when there is at least one charging, number of electric vehicles, and total energy consumption) associated with the occupancy patterns of the charging stations and to determine the typical electric vehicle charging demand profiles. The efficiency of the proposed framework has been demonstrated using a database containing information from the monitoring systems of CSs installed in a city in Spain.

articleTitle: Influence of the Mechanical Equipment on the Drive Behavior of an Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Paper concerns the behavior of a electric vehicle drive under different values of important quantity total moment of inertia. A key component in the electric drive under consideration is a newly designed battery-powered induction motor. Computer mathematical modeling has been applied, as a result of which the change in the arising torques, the flowing currents and the startup time were evaluated. As in most electric drives, the level of energy efficiency ultimately depends on their dynamic behavior. Some of the study results have been presented in tabular and graphical form. Relevant conclusions have been done.

articleTitle: Simulation and Control of a Nine Phase Induction Machine with Pole-Phase Modulation used in Propulsion System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: In these days, the automotive industry is providing a proper environment to develop and try new solutions for the electric traction systems used in the electric vehicles (EVs). One of the ideas which arose in the last years relates to the usage of different electric machine designs for obtaining the optimal value when it comes to cost-performance criteria in a drive system. From this point of view, the attention was drawn by the multiphase induction machines (MIM) which promise to fulfil the already strict requirements of the traction motor but also to add additional value when it comes to reliability and efficiency. This paper provides a technical sight of a possible way of using a MIM in a vehicle system with detailed results in the direction of field-oriented control (FOC) modelled and tested with the help of MATLAB Simulink. A pole-phase modulation control was proposed in order to adjust dynamically the desired vehicle speed on different track conditions.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of the Pressure Exerted in the Body of a High-Voltage Fuse
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Starting from the importance of high-voltage fuses on operational safety, this paper presents a study on the behavior of high-voltage fuses during short-circuit current interruption. The key element presented here is the pressure value on the fuses contacts which is commonly ignored in favor of middle element pressure. It was experimentally proven that this pressure is much higher and it is an important value for the designers. The theoretical bases and the structure of the test scheme are presented, as well as design and dimensioning elements of the high-voltage fuse components, including numerical simulations performed in the Matlab/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Influence of Thermal Agent Production Method on Thermal Energy Costs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The possibility of producing thermal energy for heating at the most advantageous price for the beneficiary of the heat, i.e. the tenant, is currently an issue not only of national interest, but also of global interest. In this paper, theoretical aspects of the type of heating installations that can be implemented in buildings and information on the algorithms for calculating heat requirements for heating and hot water preparation, currently approved in the regulations in force, are presented. The case study carried out in the paper presents the case of a condominium building (block of flats Gf+4 floors) connected to the centralised heat supply system in Craiova. For this building, the possibility of reducing the financial impact of heating the condominium dwellings was evaluated from a financial point of view, in the case of alternative heating sources.

articleTitle: Current Trends In Power Factor Compensation: Insights and Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Power factor compensation plays a crucial role in modern power systems to ensure efficient and reliable operation. This paper presents an overview of the current trends and perspectives in power factor compensation techniques. The paper discusses the importance of power factor correction in improving the power quality and optimizing energy utilization. Various methods and technologies employed for power factor compensation are explored, including passive and active approaches, as well as the utilization of advanced control algorithms and digital signal processing. The paper highlights the emerging trends in power factor compensation, such as the integration of renewable energy sources and the implementation of smart grid solutions. Furthermore, the paper addresses the challenges and opportunities in the field, including cost-effectiveness, efficiency improvement, and compliance with international standards. The paper concludes with an outlook on the future directions of power factor compensation, emphasizing the need for innovative solutions to meet the evolving demands of modern power systems.

articleTitle: Electric Discharges and Dielectric Barrier Influence on Electric Field Distribution in Solar Air Heater Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The study of electrical discharges and the breakdown manner of some dielectric materials are imperative, essentially aiming at the uniformity of the electric field that occurs between systems. The paper presents the study and simulation of the electric field in the presence of a dielectric screen, between different types of electrodes positioned on the coordinate system, by simulation in the 3D with the help of a modeling and simulation program. The work analyzes the distribution of electrical potential and electric field between electrodes type tip-plate and plate-plate, positioned on the coordinate system. Also, between tip electrode-solar air heater (SAH) panel and plate electrode-solar air heater (SAH) panel. A number of geometric factors are parameterized: the distance between the two electrodes; the displacement, thickness and radius of the dielectric barrier. The results obtained by simulation show that the geometric parameters and permittivity of the dielectric barrier have a well-determined influence on the distribution of the electric field. The presence of a dielectric screen in a range has a positive effect on the dielectric strength in the case of the positive polarity of the tip electrode and a negative effect in the case of its negative polarity. The value of the electric field decreases in direct proportion to the increase in the value of the permittivity, for a 2.1 permittivity the value of the field strength was 769.490*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>V/m, decreasing to a minimum value of 216.107*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>V/m, when the permittivity was equal to 7.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis in Electric Motors through the Analysis of Currents and Stray Fluxes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Electric motors are key assets in most industrial plants, participating in a multitude of processes and driving very diverse loads. The correct maintenance of these machines is of paramount importance, since it can avoid unplanned production stops and reduce repair costs and waiting times. Due to this, in recent years a significant effort has been devoted to the development of new predictive techniques that can improve the performance of the techniques currently used in the industry. This article reviews the most recent trends in terms of new predictive maintenance techniques based on the analysis of electrical magnitudes. More specifically, emphasis is placed on two of the technologies that have attracted most of the attention, due to their non-invasive nature, their simplicity and the valuable information they provide for diagnosis. These are techniques based on the analysis of the current demanded by the motor and the stray flux around the machine. The article reviews the fundamentals of both techniques, ranging from the most traditional variants to the most modern ones based on transient analysis. The latter have proven to be tremendously robust in reaching a fully reliable diagnosis of the failure, avoiding false indications provided by the classical variants. Two separate cases are included regarding the application of both techniques in laboratory and industrial motors. These cases help to illustrate the significant advantages that these techniques can bring. Finally, some modern systems are commented, which have been recently developed and which integrate the application of both technologies in a single device.

articleTitle: The Southern Development Region of the Republic of Moldova in Context of the Wind Energy Potential
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: One of the priority directions of the leadership of the Republic of Moldova, is the stimulation of local electricity production from renewable sources, where the main possibilities are wind and solar energy. In this paper, are studied the wind energy potential and wind characteristics for the administrative-territorial entities of the second level (districts) in the Southern Development Region of the Republic of Moldova, which includes 8 districts: Basarabeasca, Cahul, Cantemir, Căuşeni, Cimişlia, Ştefan Vodă, Leova, Taraclia and Territorial Administrative Unit - Găgăuzia. To carry out the research, were used: the special program Wind Atlas Analysis and Application Program (WASP), data on wind speed and direction measured at the hydrometeorological station Ceadir-Lunga from the subdivision of the State Hydrometeorological Service and the orographic map of the Republic of Moldova. For the whole region were: calculated and presented the maps of the average annual wind speed and wind power density at the height of 100 m above ground level; classified the district territory according to the power density value and also calculated the theoretical wind power possible to install. Following the calculations made for the eight districts analyzed and (TAU)-Găgăuzia, it was found that the average annual wind speed at a height of 100 m is between 5,27 and 7,50 m/s, and the wind power density - between 163 and 415 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. In Cantemir district was identified the highest average annual speed equal to 7,50 m/s and wind power density equal to 422 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> but in Basarabeasca district are the lowest numbers.

Author Keywords: Wind Atlas Analysis and Application Program

articleTitle: Interior Lighting, a Challenge for Yesterday's and Today's Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: There were periods when, apparently, in the interior lighting, things seemed to be resolved, clarified and nothing was necessary to investigate. Such was the long period of incandescent lamps and fluorescent lamps, burdened by the erroneous perception and understanding of Kruithoff's curve, which was contested only after half a century. The compact fluorescent lamp, which appeared next, seemed to represent a solution for energy efficiency and interior comfort. However, the negative effects of the blue components in the spectrum have been noticed. The continuous evolution of LEDs has once again changed the paradigm, and it has made necessary to continuously observe and research the physiological and psychological effects of exposure to artificial light. The main effect is the disturbance of the circadian cycle, which depends on the secretion of a specific hormone. The problem with this hormone, namely melatonin, is that it has physiological effects in the area where certain types of cancer occur, but also psychological ones, in the direction of mood, alertness, and concentration. The aim of this paper is to make an in-depth review of the existing literature on the subject of the influence of artificial lighting on human activities, with a focus on the influence of the spectral composition of LED lighting sources on learning activities in schools.

articleTitle: The Role, the Importance and Econometric Analysis of Nuclear Power Production in Romania and European Union
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: The recent energy crisis faced by many member states of the European Union has led them to postpone or even abandon the decision to phase out nuclear energy from their energy mix. Moreover, Romania is one of the member states that invest more and more in the construction of nuclear power plants. Starting from these considerations, this article provides an analysis of the current state of nuclear energy production in Romania and the European Union. Also, the article analyzes from an econometric point of view the production of nuclear energy in Romania, as well as at the level of the European Union, making forecasts for short periods of time. The forecasts obtained, highlight the importance of the continuation of nuclear energy production, in the context of the target objective of the EU-27 member states regarding energy independence.

articleTitle: Heat Pumps Use for Increasing Heat Power Plant Efficiency. A preliminary Analysis for District Heating in Bălţi City of Moldova
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Heat pumps are of major importance for the roadmap of making green heating and cooling. This is a preliminary analysis acting as a concept paper proposing steps for making greener the city heating, as part of a roadmap towards full decarbonization. In principle, for energy efficiency and the reduction of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, it is proposed to use solutions based on electricity, the most efficient option being represented by adding heat pumps for preheating the water used for district heating. The analysis has been made for the specific case of central district heating in Balti city of Moldova, with uses cases for the contribution of the heat pumps and for the source of its consumed electricity. The opportunity of adding local photovoltaic (PV) production has also been addressed and showed a significant reduction of electricity self-consumption. Conclusions and future work are also presented.

articleTitle: Modeling the Impact Produced by 400 kV Power Lines on the Environment Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electromechanical and Energy Systems (SIELMEN)
abstract: Many power plants based on renewable energy were built after Romania acceded to the EU. The produced electricity must be transported, so new 400 kV overhead power lines - OPL were developed relatively quickly. They have an impact due to the induced current on the environment, flora, and fauna. Some aspects regarding the induced effects are illustrated, based on the characteristics of the analyzed section, quantifying some essential factors with the economic aspects associated with the maintenance costs. The Cernavoda-Stalpu Section was chosen as a case study due to its problems induced by the necessity of crossing the Danube River. A multi-criteria model based on a Fuzzy tree solution is used. Applying Fuzzy logic will achieve an essential correlation between the economic and environmental protection aspects. The Fuzzy parameters were corrected and recalibrated, with a higher degree of flexibility than the classical solutions, making it easier to adapt to different changes in the OPL structures.
